entities.name: Astrocytoma, IDH-mutant
entities.anchor: IDH + TP53/ATRX; no whole-arm 1p/19q codeletion.
snv: Defining — IDH1 R132 or IDH2 R172 mutation
Cooperating — TP53 and ATRX loss-of-function mutations
cnv: Grading — CDKN2A/B homozygous deletion establishes CNS WHO grade 4
entities.pitfall: Grades 2–4 are one tumor type; an IDH-mutant grade 4 astrocytoma is not called glioblastoma.

entities.name: Oligodendroglioma, IDH-mutant and 1p/19q-codeleted
entities.anchor: Oligo = IDH + whole-arm 1p/19q loss.
snv: Defining — IDH1 or IDH2 mutation
Cooperating — TERT promoter, CIC and FUBP1 mutations
cnv: Defining — Combined whole-arm 1p and 19q deletion
entities.pitfall: Both IDH mutation and whole-arm codeletion are required; isolated/partial deletions do not qualify.

entities.name: Glioblastoma, IDH-wildtype
entities.anchor: EGFR, TERT, or +7/−10 in the appropriate adult diffuse glioma.
snv: Driver — TERT promoter and EGFR mutations (subsets)
Cooperating — PTEN, NF1, TP53 and PI3K-pathway mutations
cnv: Driver — EGFR amplification
Characteristic — Whole chromosome 7 gain with chromosome 10 loss
Cooperating — CDKN2A/B deletion; PDGFRA or CDK4 amplification (subsets)
rearr: Driver — EGFR intragenic rearrangements such as EGFRvIII; FGFR3::TACC3 (small subset)
other: Predictive biomarker — MGMT promoter methylation is epigenetic, not a defining driver.
entities.pitfall: Molecular diagnostic criteria require appropriate age, site and diffuse astrocytic context; exclude pediatric-type and other molecular gliomas.

entities.name: Diffuse midline glioma, H3 K27-altered
entities.anchor: Midline + loss of H3K27 methylation.
snv: Defining — H3-3A/H3F3A or H3C-family K27M mutation (major subset)
Driver — EGFR mutation in an alternative molecular subset
Cooperating — ACVR1, TP53, PPM1D or PI3K-pathway mutations (subsets)
other: Defining — EZHIP overexpression can produce H3K27me3 loss without an H3 mutation.
entities.pitfall: K27M alone outside a diffuse midline glioma does not establish this diagnosis. Histone legacy numbering is used.

entities.name: Diffuse hemispheric glioma, H3 G34-mutant
entities.anchor: G34 goes with hemispheres, TP53 and ATRX.
snv: Defining — H3-3A (H3F3A) G34R/V mutation
Cooperating — TP53 and ATRX loss; PDGFRA activating mutation
cnv: Cooperating — PDGFRA amplification; CDKN2A/B deletion (subsets)
entities.pitfall: This is a distinct pediatric-type high-grade glioma, including cases in adults; histone legacy G34 numbering is used.

entities.name: Diffuse pediatric-type high-grade glioma, H3-wildtype and IDH-wildtype
entities.anchor: Pediatric H3/IDH-wildtype high-grade tumors need a positive molecular identity.
snv: Cooperating — TP53 or other pathway mutations (variable)
cnv: Driver — PDGFRA, EGFR or MYCN amplification in associated molecular groups
other: Defining context — Appropriate methylation class supports diagnosis; RTK1, RTK2 and MYCN-associated groups exist.
entities.pitfall: H3-wildtype plus IDH-wildtype alone is insufficient; this is not simply childhood glioblastoma.

entities.name: Infant-type hemispheric glioma
entities.anchor: Infant hemispheric glioma: look for a kinase fusion.
rearr: Driver — ALK, NTRK1/2/3, ROS1 or MET fusion (alternative subsets)
entities.pitfall: Fusion partner varies; absence of a detectable kinase fusion does not by itself exclude the integrated entity.

entities.name: High-grade astrocytoma with piloid features
entities.anchor: MAPK activation + CDKN2A/B loss + a defining methylation profile.
snv: Driver — NF1, BRAF or FGFR1 pathway mutation (alternative subsets)
Cooperating — ATRX mutation
cnv: Cooperating — CDKN2A/B homozygous deletion
rearr: Driver — BRAF or other MAPK-pathway fusion (subset)
other: Defining — DNA methylation profile is essential to this entity.
entities.pitfall: Piloid morphology or a MAPK mutation alone does not establish HGAP.

entities.name: Pleomorphic xanthoastrocytoma
entities.anchor: PXA pairs BRAF/RAF activation with CDKN2A/B loss.
snv: Driver — BRAF V600E (common subset)
Cooperating — TERT promoter mutation (especially higher-grade tumors)
cnv: Cooperating — CDKN2A/B homozygous deletion
rearr: Driver — BRAF or RAF1 fusion/rearrangement (alternative subset)
entities.pitfall: Includes grades 2 and 3; grade 2 does not mean a benign tumor. Molecular findings overlap with other gliomas.

entities.name: Astroblastoma, MN1-altered
entities.anchor: Astroblastoma: MN1 rearrangement.
rearr: Defining — MN1 rearrangement, usually MN1::BEND2; MN1::CXXC5 in a subset
other: Classification — DNA methylation helps resolve histologic mimics.
entities.pitfall: Astroblastic architecture is not specific; molecular identity matters. A uniform CNS WHO grade is not assigned.

entities.name: Diffuse leptomeningeal glioneuronal tumor
entities.anchor: MAPK fusion + 1p loss, without IDH mutation.
cnv: Characteristic — 1p loss; 1q gain marks an important molecular subset
rearr: Driver — KIAA1549::BRAF (common); other MAPK-pathway fusions in subsets
other: Classification — Distinct methylation groups; malignant behavior coding does not imply uniformly high-grade histology.
entities.pitfall: Some tumors initially lack diffuse leptomeningeal spread. Do not call this oligodendroglioma from 1p loss alone.

entities.name: Ependymoma
entities.anchor: Supratentorial fusions; posterior fossa epigenetics; spinal NF2/MYCN.
snv: Driver — NF2 loss-of-function (spinal subset)
cnv: Defining — MYCN amplification in spinal ependymoma, MYCN-amplified
Characteristic — 22q loss in spinal tumors; 1q gain in subsets
rearr: Defining — ZFTA::RELA or other ZFTA fusion; YAP1::MAMLD1 or other YAP1 fusion (separate supratentorial types)
other: Defining — Posterior fossa PFA/PFB methylation groups; PFA commonly shows EZHIP-associated H3K27me3 loss.
entities.pitfall: These alterations describe alternative WHO entities within the broad family, not one co-occurring panel. Subependymoma is excluded.

entities.name: Choroid plexus carcinoma
entities.anchor: Choroid plexus carcinoma: remember TP53.
snv: Driver — TP53 inactivation (somatic or germline-associated subset)
cnv: Characteristic — Complex chromosome gains and losses
entities.pitfall: TP53-wildtype cases occur; a tumor TP53 variant alone does not prove a germline syndrome.

entities.name: Medulloblastoma
entities.anchor: WNT→CTNNB1; SHH→PTCH1/SMO/SUFU; group 3/4→MYC-family and chromatin.
snv: Driver — CTNNB1 activation or APC loss (WNT)
Driver — PTCH1, SUFU or SMO mutation (SHH); TP53 defines a key SHH subset
Driver/cooperating — KBTBD4 insertions and chromatin-regulator mutations (non-WNT/non-SHH subsets)
cnv: Characteristic — Monosomy 6 (WNT subset)
Driver — MYC amplification (group 3 enriched); MYCN or CDK6 amplification (subsets)
Characteristic — Isochromosome 17q (non-WNT/non-SHH enriched)
rearr: Driver — Enhancer-hijacking rearrangements involving GFI1/GFI1B or PRDM6 (subsets)
other: Defining — Molecular groups are integrated with methylation/expression findings.
entities.pitfall: No single mutation covers every medulloblastoma; group names are not interchangeable with histologic patterns.

entities.name: Atypical teratoid/rhabdoid tumor
entities.anchor: ATRT = SWI/SNF loss, usually SMARCB1.
snv: Defining — Biallelic SMARCB1 inactivation; rare SMARCA4-inactivated tumors
cnv: Defining — SMARCB1 deletion is a common inactivation mechanism
rearr: Defining — Structural disruption of SMARCB1 (subset)
other: Classification — Epigenetic groups exist despite few additional recurrent mutations.
entities.pitfall: Loss of INI1/SMARCB1 protein is a clue, not itself a DNA deletion result; other tumor types also lose SMARCB1.

entities.name: Embryonal tumor with multilayered rosettes
entities.anchor: ETMR: microRNA machinery—C19MC or DICER1.
snv: Driver — DICER1 alterations in a subset without C19MC amplification
cnv: Driver — C19MC microRNA-cluster amplification; MIR17HG amplification in rare alternative cases
rearr: Driver — C19MC-region rearrangement, including TTYH1::C19MC-associated events
entities.pitfall: C19MC amplification is not universal. Historical CNS medulloepithelioma/ependymoblastoma patterns overlap this family.

entities.name: CNS neuroblastoma, FOXR2-activated
entities.anchor: CNS FOXR2 is different from peripheral ALK/MYCN neuroblastoma.
cnv: Characteristic — Chromosome 1q gain
rearr: Driver — Structural events activating FOXR2 (variable architecture)
other: Defining — FOXR2 activation with an appropriate methylation profile.
entities.pitfall: FOXR2 expression/activation is the key; a single fixed fusion partner is not required.

entities.name: CNS tumor with BCOR internal tandem duplication
entities.anchor: CNS BCOR tumor: exon 15 internal tandem duplication.
snv: Defining — BCOR exon 15 internal tandem duplication (ITD)
entities.pitfall: BCOR immunostaining alone does not prove an ITD; BCOR fusions in other sarcomas are different alterations.

entities.name: CNS embryonal tumor, NOS/NEC
entities.anchor: Unresolved embryonal category: no universal genetic driver.
other: Unresolved — Molecular workup has not assigned a recognized specific embryonal entity.
entities.pitfall: NOS reflects missing/insufficient classification information; NEC reflects an investigated tumor outside established entities. Not one molecular disease.

entities.name: Pineoblastoma
entities.anchor: Pineoblastoma: microRNA processing, RB1, or MYC/FOXR2.
snv: Driver — DICER1, DROSHA or DGCR8 defects (miRNA-associated groups)
Driver — RB1 inactivation (RB-associated group)
cnv: Driver — DROSHA/DGCR8 or RB1 loss; MYC amplification (group-dependent)
other: Classification — MYC/FOXR2 activation and distinct methylation groups are important.
entities.pitfall: Listed abnormalities belong to alternative groups; not every pineoblastoma is DICER1-mutant.

entities.name: Pineal parenchymal tumor of intermediate differentiation
entities.anchor: PPTID: KBTBD4 insertion.
snv: Driver — Recurrent small in-frame KBTBD4 insertion (subset)
entities.pitfall: “Intermediate differentiation” is the entity name, not synonymous with benign/intermediate behavior. No single mutation fully grades it.

entities.name: Papillary tumor of the pineal region
entities.anchor: Papillary pineal tumor: chromosome 10 loss; PTEN in a subset.
snv: Driver — PTEN inactivation (subset)
cnv: Characteristic — Chromosome 10 loss
other: Classification — Distinct DNA methylation profile.
entities.pitfall: PTEN mutations are variable across cohorts; chromosome 10 loss is not uniquely diagnostic.

entities.name: Meningioma, CNS WHO grade 3
entities.anchor: Grade 3 molecular flags: TERT promoter or CDKN2A/B homozygous loss.
snv: Grading — TERT promoter mutation
Driver/cooperating — NF2 or BAP1 inactivation (subsets)
cnv: Grading — CDKN2A and/or CDKN2B homozygous deletion
Characteristic — Accumulated chromosomal losses in aggressive tumors
entities.pitfall: Only grade 3 is included here. Grade 3 can be assigned by histology or qualifying molecular findings; rhabdoid morphology alone is insufficient.

entities.name: Primary intracranial sarcoma, DICER1-mutant
entities.anchor: Intracranial sarcoma: DICER1 plus MAPK/TP53.
snv: Defining — DICER1 RNase IIIb hotspot mutation, often with second-allele inactivation
Cooperating — TP53; KRAS or NF1 pathway alterations (subsets)
entities.pitfall: A DICER1 alteration must be interpreted with histology/site and methylation classification; tumor-only findings do not establish germline status.

entities.name: Liposarcoma
entities.anchor: Three routes: MDM2 amplification, DDIT3 fusion, or complex TP53/RB1 damage.
snv: Cooperating — TP53 and ATRX alterations (pleomorphic/myxoid pleomorphic subsets)
Cooperating — TERT promoter and PIK3CA alterations (myxoid subset)
cnv: Defining — MDM2 amplification, often with CDK4 (well-differentiated/dedifferentiated)
Cooperating — RB1 loss (pleomorphic/myxoid pleomorphic subsets)
rearr: Defining — FUS::DDIT3 or EWSR1::DDIT3 (myxoid)
entities.pitfall: Keep the molecular subsets separate in memory. Atypical lipomatous tumor is an intermediate counterpart and is outside the malignant-only scope.

entities.name: Leiomyosarcoma
entities.anchor: Smooth muscle sarcoma: TP53, RB1, ATRX; complex genome.
snv: Driver/cooperating — TP53, RB1, ATRX and PTEN inactivation (subsets)
cnv: Cooperating — RB1/PTEN loss; MYOCD amplification (subset)
entities.pitfall: No universal defining fusion. Covers soft tissue, uterine and primary bone sites; the inflammatory subtype has distinctive near-haploid genomes.

entities.name: Rhabdomyosarcoma
entities.anchor: RMS: FOXO1 fusion, RAS pathway, or MYOD1.
snv: Driver — HRAS/KRAS/NRAS, FGFR4 or PIK3CA activation (fusion-negative subsets)
Driver — MYOD1 L122R (spindle/sclerosing subset)
Cooperating — TP53; DICER1 in selected anatomic subsets
cnv: Cooperating — 11p15 allelic imbalance; MYCN/CDK4 amplification (subsets)
rearr: Defining — PAX3::FOXO1 or PAX7::FOXO1 (fusion-positive subset)
Driver — VGLL2/NCOA2-associated fusions in infantile spindle-cell tumors; TFCP2 fusions in a rare intraosseous subset
entities.pitfall: Broad family includes embryonal, alveolar, pleomorphic and spindle/sclerosing tumors. Histologic alveolar appearance is not equivalent to FOXO1 fusion.

entities.name: Solitary fibrous tumor, malignant/high-risk
entities.anchor: Solitary fibrous tumor: NAB2::STAT6.
rearr: Defining — NAB2::STAT6
entities.pitfall: The fusion identifies the tumor family, not malignant behavior; risk assessment remains clinicopathologic. Includes malignant CNS SFT.

entities.name: Adult-type fibrosarcoma / fibrosarcoma of bone
entities.anchor: A diagnosis of exclusion; no universal molecular hallmark.
other: Unresolved — No established recurrent defining driver for conventional adult-type fibrosarcoma.
entities.pitfall: Exclude fusion-defined mimics and other differentiated sarcomas before using this diagnosis.

entities.name: Low-grade myofibroblastic sarcoma
entities.anchor: Myofibroblastic morphology; no established signature driver.
other: Unresolved — No established recurrent defining molecular alteration.
entities.pitfall: Do not transfer ALK fusions from inflammatory myofibroblastic tumor to this different entity.

entities.name: Myxofibrosarcoma
entities.anchor: Complex genome: TP53/RB1/CDKN2A pathways.
snv: Driver/cooperating — TP53 and other tumor-suppressor mutations
cnv: Cooperating — RB1, CDKN2A/B or TP53 loss; complex gains/losses
entities.pitfall: No single pathognomonic fusion; overlaps genomically with undifferentiated pleomorphic sarcoma.

entities.name: Low-grade fibromyxoid sarcoma
aliases: Hyalinizing spindle cell tumor with giant rosettes
entities.anchor: Fibromyxoid + FUS::CREB3L2.
rearr: Defining — FUS::CREB3L2; FUS::CREB3L1 in a smaller subset
entities.pitfall: Bland histology does not imply benign behavior; hybrid LGFMS/SEF can share the FUS-associated profile.

entities.name: Sclerosing epithelioid fibrosarcoma
entities.anchor: Sclerosing epithelioid sarcoma: EWSR1::CREB3L1.
rearr: Defining — EWSR1::CREB3L1 (common); EWSR1::CREB3L2 (subset)
Defining — FUS::CREB3L2 in some hybrid LGFMS/SEF tumors
entities.pitfall: MUC4 expression is an immunophenotypic clue, not a mutation; pure SEF and LGFMS have different fusion enrichments.

entities.name: Infantile fibrosarcoma
entities.anchor: Infantile fibrosarcoma: ETV6::NTRK3.
rearr: Defining — ETV6::NTRK3 (typical)
Driver — Alternative NTRK or other kinase fusions in related fusion-negative tumors
entities.pitfall: ETV6::NTRK3 is shared by several other entities; age, site and histology remain necessary.

entities.name: NTRK-rearranged spindle cell neoplasm, malignant
entities.anchor: Malignant spindle cells + an NTRK fusion.
rearr: Driver — NTRK1, NTRK2 or NTRK3 fusion; examples include LMNA::NTRK1 and TPM3::NTRK1
entities.pitfall: WHO5 emerging category; only malignant examples are included. Pan-TRK staining is not proof of a fusion.

entities.name: Angiosarcoma
entities.anchor: Vascular sarcoma: MYC amplification or vascular/MAPK pathway mutations.
snv: Driver — KDR, PLCG1, PTPRB or RAS/MAPK-pathway mutations (subsets)
Cooperating — TP53 mutation
cnv: Driver — MYC amplification, especially radiation/lymphedema-associated tumors
Cooperating — FLT4 amplification; CDKN2A loss (subsets)
entities.pitfall: MYC amplification is not universal. Includes primary cutaneous, visceral and bone angiosarcoma.

entities.name: Epithelioid hemangioendothelioma
entities.anchor: EHE: WWTR1::CAMTA1; TFE3-associated alternative.
rearr: Defining — WWTR1::CAMTA1
Defining — YAP1::TFE3 in a distinct related molecular subset
entities.pitfall: A malignant vascular tumor despite sometimes indolent behavior; covers soft tissue, bone, lung and liver sites.

entities.name: Malignant peripheral nerve sheath tumor
entities.anchor: NF1 + CDKN2A loss + PRC2 loss.
snv: Driver — NF1 inactivation
Cooperating — SUZ12, EED and TP53 inactivation (subsets)
cnv: Cooperating — CDKN2A/B deletion; SUZ12/EED loss
Driver — SMARCB1 deletion/inactivation in an epithelioid subset
other: Surrogate — H3K27me3 loss reflects PRC2 disruption in many conventional tumors.
entities.pitfall: H3K27me3 loss is neither universal nor absolutely specific. Epithelioid MPNST can have different biology.

entities.name: Malignant melanotic nerve sheath tumor
entities.anchor: Pigmented nerve sheath tumor: PRKAR1A.
snv: Driver — PRKAR1A loss-of-function mutation
cnv: Cooperating — Chromosome 17 loss/PRKAR1A allelic loss (subset)
entities.pitfall: Formerly melanotic schwannoma; distinct from conventional schwannoma and melanoma. Can be associated with Carney complex.

entities.name: Myoepithelial carcinoma of soft tissue/bone
entities.anchor: Soft tissue myoepithelial carcinoma often uses EWSR1 partners.
cnv: Driver — SMARCB1 deletion/inactivation (subset)
rearr: Driver — EWSR1::POU5F1; other EWSR1/FUS fusions including PBX1, PBX3 or KLF17 partners (subsets)
entities.pitfall: A fusion does not prove malignancy; histology establishes carcinoma. Salivary gland myoepithelial tumors have a different molecular spectrum.

entities.name: Synovial sarcoma
entities.anchor: Synovial sarcoma: SS18::SSX.
rearr: Defining — SS18::SSX1 or SS18::SSX2; rare SS18::SSX4
entities.pitfall: The name does not imply origin from synovium; occurs at many sites.

entities.name: Epithelioid sarcoma
entities.anchor: Epithelioid sarcoma: SMARCB1/INI1 loss.
snv: Driver — SMARCB1 inactivating variants (subset)
cnv: Driver — SMARCB1 homozygous deletion (common mechanism)
other: Surrogate — INI1 protein loss is characteristic.
entities.pitfall: SMARCB1 loss also occurs in several other tumors; it is not sufficient alone for diagnosis.

entities.name: Alveolar soft part sarcoma
entities.anchor: ASPS: ASPSCR1::TFE3.
rearr: Defining — ASPSCR1::TFE3
entities.pitfall: The same fusion can occur in TFE3-rearranged renal cell carcinoma; site and phenotype matter.

entities.name: Clear cell sarcoma of soft tissue
aliases: Clear cell sarcoma of tendons and aponeuroses
entities.anchor: Melanocytic-looking sarcoma: EWSR1::ATF1.
rearr: Defining — EWSR1::ATF1; EWSR1::CREB1 in a subset
entities.pitfall: Do not equate it with cutaneous melanoma or gastrointestinal neuroectodermal tumor.

entities.name: Extraskeletal myxoid chondrosarcoma
entities.anchor: The name says cartilage; the defining gene is NR4A3.
rearr: Defining — EWSR1::NR4A3; TAF15::NR4A3 and rarer NR4A3 partners
entities.pitfall: Not a conventional cartilage-producing chondrosarcoma; EWSR1-negative results do not exclude a variant NR4A3 fusion.

entities.name: Desmoplastic small round cell tumor
entities.anchor: DSRCT: EWSR1::WT1.
rearr: Defining — EWSR1::WT1
entities.pitfall: WT1 immunostaining alone is not the fusion; additional recurrent mutations are uncommon.

entities.name: Malignant rhabdoid tumor, extrarenal
entities.anchor: Rhabdoid tumor: lose SMARCB1.
snv: Defining — Biallelic SMARCB1 inactivation; rarely SMARCA4 inactivation
cnv: Defining — SMARCB1 deletion (frequent mechanism)
rearr: Defining — SMARCB1 structural disruption (subset)
entities.pitfall: Rhabdoid morphology occurs in many unrelated cancers; renal rhabdoid tumor and CNS ATRT are covered separately.

entities.name: PEComa, malignant
entities.anchor: PEComa: TSC–mTOR or TFE3.
snv: Driver — TSC1 or TSC2 loss-of-function
cnv: Driver — TSC1/TSC2 deletion (subset)
rearr: Driver — TFE3 fusion, e.g. SFPQ::TFE3 (alternative subset)
Driver — RAD51B-associated fusion (rare uterine subset)
entities.pitfall: Molecular route does not by itself establish malignant behavior; benign angiomyolipoma and LAM are excluded.

entities.name: Intimal sarcoma
entities.anchor: Intimal sarcoma: MDM2, often CDK4/PDGFRA.
cnv: Driver — MDM2 amplification
Cooperating — CDK4 and/or PDGFRA amplification (subsets)
entities.pitfall: A vascular/cardiac sarcoma with variable morphology; MDM2 amplification alone is not site-specific.

entities.name: Undifferentiated sarcoma
entities.anchor: A complex-genome category after excluding a specific lineage.
snv: Driver/cooperating — TP53 and other tumor-suppressor mutations
cnv: Cooperating — RB1, CDKN2A/B or TP53 loss; complex copy-number alterations
entities.pitfall: Includes undifferentiated pleomorphic sarcoma of soft tissue/bone; fusion-defined round cell sarcomas have separate entries.

entities.name: Ewing sarcoma
entities.anchor: Ewing = FET-family gene + ETS-family transcription factor.
snv: Cooperating — STAG2 and TP53 mutations (subsets)
cnv: Cooperating — CDKN2A deletion (subset)
rearr: Defining — EWSR1::FLI1 or EWSR1::ERG; rarer FET::ETS alternatives
entities.pitfall: An EWSR1 rearrangement alone is not Ewing sarcoma; the partner matters.

entities.name: Round cell sarcoma with EWSR1–non-ETS fusions
entities.anchor: EWSR1 + a non-ETS partner is a different family.
cnv: Characteristic — Amplification of the rearranged EWSR1 region in NFATC2-associated cases (subset)
rearr: Defining — EWSR1::NFATC2 or EWSR1::PATZ1; related FUS::NFATC2 tumors
entities.pitfall: These are molecularly heterogeneous tumors; do not relabel every EWSR1 fusion tumor into this group.

entities.name: CIC-rearranged sarcoma
entities.anchor: CIC sarcoma: usually CIC::DUX4.
rearr: Defining — CIC::DUX4; alternative CIC partners including NUTM1 or FOXO4 (rare)
entities.pitfall: Distinct from Ewing sarcoma; DUX4-region repetitive sequence can complicate fusion detection.

entities.name: Sarcoma with BCOR genetic alterations
entities.anchor: BCOR sarcoma: CCNB3 fusion or BCOR ITD.
snv: Defining — BCOR internal tandem duplication (subset)
rearr: Defining — BCOR::CCNB3; other BCOR fusions (subsets)
Related molecular subset — YWHAE::NUTM2B/E in infantile round cell sarcoma
entities.pitfall: BCOR protein expression is not specific; CNS BCOR-ITD tumors and renal clear cell sarcoma are listed separately.

entities.name: Osteosarcoma
entities.anchor: Osteoid + disrupted TP53/RB1; low-grade central/parosteal often MDM2.
snv: Driver/cooperating — TP53, RB1 and ATRX inactivation
cnv: Driver — MDM2 and CDK4 amplification (especially low-grade central/parosteal and their dedifferentiated forms)
Cooperating — Complex amplifications/deletions in conventional high-grade tumors
rearr: Driver — TP53-disrupting structural rearrangements (subset)
entities.pitfall: No universal oncogenic fusion; includes central and surface histologic patterns. Osteoid production must be by tumor cells.

entities.name: Extraskeletal osteosarcoma
entities.anchor: Soft tissue osteoid-producing sarcoma with a complex genome.
snv: Driver/cooperating — TP53/RB-pathway alterations (subsets)
cnv: Cooperating — Complex copy-number changes; MDM2/CDK4 amplification in a subset
entities.pitfall: Exclude a skeletal primary and dedifferentiated liposarcoma with osteosarcomatous differentiation.

entities.name: Chondrosarcoma
entities.anchor: Central: IDH; peripheral: EXT lineage; mesenchymal: HEY1::NCOA2.
snv: Driver — IDH1/IDH2 hotspot mutation (central conventional/dedifferentiated subsets)
Lineage-associated — EXT1/EXT2 inactivation in osteochondroma-associated peripheral tumors
Cooperating — TP53 and TERT promoter mutations (especially progression/dedifferentiation)
cnv: Cooperating — CDKN2A/B deletion (subsets)
rearr: Defining — HEY1::NCOA2 (mesenchymal subset)
entities.pitfall: Clear cell and some periosteal tumors lack a consistent hallmark. EXT alterations alone indicate the precursor pathway, not malignant transformation.

entities.name: Chordoma
entities.anchor: Brachyury lineage; CDKN2A loss; poorly differentiated tumors lose SMARCB1.
snv: Cooperating — PBRM1 or other chromatin-regulator alterations (subsets)
cnv: Driver/cooperating — CDKN2A/B loss; TBXT amplification (subsets)
Defining — SMARCB1 loss in poorly differentiated chordoma
entities.pitfall: Brachyury protein expression is a lineage marker and does not automatically mean TBXT amplification.

entities.name: Adamantinoma of long bones
entities.anchor: Adamantinoma: no established universal genomic hallmark.
snv: Candidate/cooperating — KMT2D alterations reported in a small molecular series
other: Evidence — Genomic series remain small; no defining driver established.
entities.pitfall: Not ameloblastoma of the jaw. Osteofibrous dysplasia-like lesions have different behavior and are outside this malignant entry.

entities.name: Malignant giant cell tumor of bone
entities.anchor: H3.3 G34W marks the lineage, not malignancy.
snv: Lineage-associated driver — H3-3A/H3F3A G34W (often retained, sometimes lost in malignant progression)
entities.pitfall: H3F3A G34W also occurs in ordinary intermediate GCTB; malignancy requires a sarcomatous component. Some malignant components are mutation-negative.

entities.name: Glomus tumor, malignant
entities.anchor: Malignant glomus tumor often carries a NOTCH fusion.
rearr: Driver — MIR143/CARMN::NOTCH2; other NOTCH-family fusions (subsets)
entities.pitfall: The same fusion class occurs in benign glomus tumors and cannot define malignant behavior.

entities.name: Ossifying fibromyxoid tumor, malignant
entities.anchor: Ossifying fibromyxoid tumor: PHF1-associated fusion.
rearr: Driver — EP400::PHF1, MEAF6::PHF1 or EPC1::PHF1 (subsets)
Driver — Other fusions, including ZC3H7B::BCOR (rare)
entities.pitfall: Fusions are shared with nonmalignant OFMT and some other tumor families; histology establishes malignancy.

entities.name: Phosphaturic mesenchymal tumor, malignant
entities.anchor: Phosphaturic tumor: FGF signaling fusion.
rearr: Driver — FN1::FGFR1; FN1::FGF1 in the broader PMT family
other: Functional output — FGF23 secretion can cause tumor-induced osteomalacia.
entities.pitfall: Only malignant PMT is included; these fusions do not independently distinguish benign from malignant tumors.

entities.name: Granular cell tumor, malignant
entities.anchor: Rare malignant granular cell tumor: no validated universal driver.
other: Unresolved — No established malignancy-specific recurrent genomic hallmark; published sequencing cohorts are very small.
entities.pitfall: Do not promote an isolated case mutation to a universal driver or infer malignancy from mutations found in benign granular cell tumors.

entities.name: Ectomesenchymoma
entities.anchor: Rhabdomyoblastic + neural elements; often HRAS.
snv: Driver — HRAS activating mutation (recurrent in small series)
entities.pitfall: An exceptionally rare mixed tumor; HRAS is not specific and overlaps embryonal rhabdomyosarcoma.

entities.name: Neuroblastoma / ganglioneuroblastoma
entities.anchor: Neuroblastoma: ALK, MYCN, or telomere maintenance.
snv: Driver — ALK activating mutation
Driver/cooperating — ATRX, PTPN11 or RAS-pathway alteration (subsets)
cnv: Driver — MYCN amplification; ALK amplification (subset)
Characteristic — 1p/11q loss and 17q gain (subsets)
rearr: Driver — TERT enhancer-associated rearrangement (subset)
other: Mechanism — ATRX loss can support alternative lengthening of telomeres.
entities.pitfall: Many tumors have few coding mutations. Ganglioneuroblastoma is retained in this broad peripheral neuroblastic family; benign ganglioneuroma is excluded.

entities.name: Uveal melanoma
entities.anchor: Uveal: GNAQ/GNA11, then BAP1/SF3B1/EIF1AX.
snv: Driver — GNAQ or GNA11; less often CYSLTR2 or PLCB4
Cooperating/classifying — BAP1, SF3B1 or EIF1AX mutations
cnv: Cooperating — Monosomy 3/BAP1 allelic loss; chromosome 8q gain (subsets)
entities.pitfall: Uveal and conjunctival melanomas have different driver spectra; BRAF is not the usual uveal driver.

entities.name: Retinoblastoma
entities.anchor: Retinoblastoma: two-hit RB1; rare MYCN-driven alternative.
snv: Defining driver — Biallelic RB1 inactivation
Cooperating — BCOR or CREBBP mutation (subsets)
cnv: Driver — RB1 deletion; MYCN amplification (subset, occasionally RB1-intact)
rearr: Driver — RB1-disrupting structural rearrangements
other: Driver mechanism — RB1 promoter methylation or copy-neutral loss of heterozygosity can provide an inactivating hit.
entities.pitfall: A tumor RB1 event is not automatically germline; routine small-variant sequencing can miss structural/epigenetic hits.

entities.name: Medulloepithelioma of ciliary body, malignant
entities.anchor: Intraocular medulloepithelioma: remember DICER1.
snv: Driver — DICER1 mutation (subset)
Candidate/cooperating — KMT2D mutation (subset)
entities.pitfall: Only malignant cases are in scope. Ocular medulloepithelioma is not equivalent to CNS ETMR.

entities.name: Prostatic stromal sarcoma
entities.anchor: Specialized prostatic stromal sarcoma has no universal driver.
other: Unresolved — Marked molecular heterogeneity; no established defining recurrent alteration.
entities.pitfall: Some presumed cases are reclassified after detecting a fusion characteristic of another sarcoma. Do not transfer findings from one case to the whole entity.

entities.name: Odontogenic sarcoma
entities.anchor: Odontogenic sarcoma: BRAF/MAPK in the malignant mesenchymal component.
snv: Driver — BRAF V600E; NRAS mutation in an alternative small subset
entities.pitfall: Rare-tumor evidence comes from small series; benign epithelial islands are part of the biphasic tumor.

entities.name: Odontogenic carcinosarcoma
entities.anchor: Both epithelial and mesenchymal components are malignant.
other: Unresolved — No established recurrent defining molecular driver.
entities.pitfall: Do not automatically assign the BRAF frequency of odontogenic sarcoma to this much rarer separate entity.

coverage.basis: WHO fifth-edition structures for CNS, soft tissue/bone and eye/orbit; broad malignant families, with molecularly distinct CNS/round-cell sarcoma entities retained. Malignant behavior is not synonymous with high histologic grade.
merged: Medulloblastoma molecular groups are internal alternatives within one broad row.
Ependymoma anatomic/molecular entities are internal alternatives within one row; nonmalignant subependymoma and myxopapillary ependymoma are excluded.
Liposarcoma, rhabdomyosarcoma, chondrosarcoma, osteosarcoma and chordoma histologic subsets are listed within broad rows.
Soft tissue, bone and visceral presentations of the same sarcoma family are combined, except when site changes molecular identity.
Peripheral neuroblastoma and ganglioneuroblastoma are combined.
excluded: Benign and intermediate tumors: ordinary schwannoma/neurofibroma, grade 1–2 meningioma, pilocytic astrocytoma, most low-grade glioneuronal tumors, desmoid fibromatosis, ordinary giant cell tumor of bone, angiomatoid fibrous histiocytoma, conventional inflammatory myofibroblastic tumor, pseudomyogenic hemangioendothelioma, and other intermediate vascular/fibroblastic entities.
Provisional CNS DGONC, cribriform neuroepithelial tumor, FET::CREB intracranial mesenchymal tumor and desmoplastic myxoid pineal tumor are not automatically treated as established malignant entities.

CNS/ocular lymphomas and histiocytic neoplasms are covered with hematolymphoid tumors. CNS germ-cell tumors, renal embryonal tumors, GIST, epithelial/melanocytic skin/conjunctival tumors, salivary/lacrimal carcinomas and pituitary malignancies are covered in their respective organ families.
limitations: This is an educational broad-family crosswalk, not a verbatim WHO taxonomy or an exhaustive list of every reported genomic alteration.
Evidence for exceptionally rare sarcomas may be limited to small cohorts; candidate findings are labeled and no fixed prevalence is implied.
Molecular grouping evolves; WHO5 emerging/provisional categories and behavior-code differences need explicit contextual interpretation.
A mutation, amplification, fusion or immunostain rarely proves tumor type without histology and clinical context.
